Thanks again for the demo today — great discussion and appreciate the clarity on your use cases (clinical notes indexing + patient Q&A). Per our conversation, I wanted to put together the immediate follow-ups and a concise set of asks so we can keep momentum for the PoC.

Action items for Amaya:
- Confirm SOC 2 status and whether you need Redwood to provide a recent SOC 2 Type II report or an SOC 2 letter of attestation.
- Confirm whether HIPAA/business associate agreement is required for the PoC (we can scope encryption/KMS and logging accordingly).
- Complete the attached vendor security questionnaire (we pre-filled some fields) and return — marked sheet tabs: "Data Retention" and "Backups".

From our side (what to expect):
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report; I attached the security pack and can provide a redacted report via our secure share once NDA is in place.
- Data retention/deletion: Our standard hosted offering supports configurable retention windows; default log retention is 90 days, with options for 30/365 depending on contract. Backups are retained separately; we can align backup deletion to match primary deletion SLA with appropriate change controls.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data residency, field-level encryption, and can sign a BAA.

Please see the attached Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Amaya.xlsx — we've prefilled some answers under the "Retention" tab to speed things up. If you can return by Friday, 21 May, we'll have security and legal review ready to lock the PoC onboarding schedule.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the assets — super helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before we send the completed questionnaire:

1) SOC 2: We are evaluating vendors and prefer a full SOC 2 Type II report where available. If you can provide a redacted PDF through the secure share (and confirm the audit period), that would help our security team.

2) Deletion SLAs: For clinical identifiers and PHI-derived material we need a 30-day deletion SLA for primary data and 90 days for backups — policy reasoned by our backup retention and restore window. Is that something Redwood can accommodate?

3) Log retention: We need more detail on what you retain in logs (request/response bodies, user identifiers, client IPs). Specifically: do you persist full request/response payloads in logs and for how long?

4) HIPAA BAAs: yes, we'll require a BAA for the PoC. Can you share a standard BAA (or tell me the process/timeline)?

Hi Samir / Marissa —

Following up with the security details requested below. Summaries here; attaching the fuller security pack.

SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II for the period Jan 2026–Dec 2026. We can provide a redacted PDF through our secure file share (DocuSign/ShareFile) after a standard NDA — typical turnaround 24–48 hours.

Deletion SLAs / Backups:
- Primary data deletion: we support configurable deletion policies. Standard SLA options: 30, 90, 180 days. We can contractually commit to 30-day deletion for primary data.
- Backups: backups are retained in a separate lifecycle; default snapshot retention is 90 days. We can align backup retention to 90 days and implement a policy to purge backup snapshots older than 90 days. If Amaya requires backup purging faster than 90 days, that will affect our restore window and requires ops coordination; we can accommodate but may need an exception approval during onboarding.

Log Retention:
- Audit logs: retained 365 days by default (configurable).
- Application logs: default 90 days; can be reduced to 30 days for customers with contractual needs.
- Request/response bodies: for hosted API, request bodies are not stored in plaintext logs by default. We persist request metadata (timestamp, model, client_id, token usage) and error traces; request/response payloads are only retained if the customer enables full request logging for debugging. For PoC we recommend disabling full body logging unless needed.

HIPAA / BAA: we are BAA-ready; our legal team provides a standard BAA template and typical turnaround for review is 5–7 business days after request.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa: share the redacted SOC 2 via secure share (I can help enable access).
2) Samir / Priya: return the questionnaire with the 30-day primary / 90-day backup preference noted.
3) Rishi (included): we'll prepare a short addendum to the MSA that calls out retention SLAs and backup retention mapping for the PoC.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Pack_v2.pdf (full pack)

-Neha
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Hi Samir / team —

Quick answers to the two items you called out:

1) Backups & keys: For PoC we can offer platform-managed KMS by default. We also support BYOK (customer-managed keys) for production or regulated workloads. For Amaya's PoC (PHI), we can enable BYOK — we'll need a short onboarding window to exchange key material and update the backup encryption configuration (typical timeline 2–3 business days).

2) Temporary full-request logging + purge workflow:
- Process: we create a short-lived logging profile for the PoC environment and enable full request/response capture only for a defined time window.
- Purge: we will configure an automated lifecycle job to purge captured bodies after 30 days; job runs daily and marks data for permanent deletion. We will include this in the onboarding SOW and provide a one-time operational sign-off from Ops.

If that aligns, Marissa — can you confirm acceptance and I will draft a 1-page addendum to the SOW that details: BYOK setup steps, logging profile creation, and the 30-day purge automation (ops sign-off). I will attach the retention matrix (Retention-Retention-Matrix.csv) to the addendum.

Thanks,
